data.text: Rejected-before measured on this repository's journal: ten prompts that propose a rejected alternative (embeddings in the core, a validation library, an async core, committing state.json, velocity as a mean, a delete that erases, rejecting the later event, a PreToolUse hook on grep, hooks only where .claude exists, auto-commit) and ten ordinary code prompts. REJECTED_SHARE 0.35: 8/10 named the right decision, 0 named another, 0/10 false alarms. 0.25: 8/10 but one false alarm; 0.5: 6/10. Misses are vocabulary - 'async' vs 'asynchronous', 'erase' vs 'erases' - which light stemming (KAD-69) may close. The hook went from ~140 to ~165 ms: rejectedMatches builds a second index for the query terms; sharing it with search is the obvious saving if it matters. Seen to fail first: the new hook test returned nothing for 'a single tasks.json file'.
